content.text:
The bug was in `saveAll` in `store.js`. It called `items.forEach(async ...)`, and `forEach` doesn't wait for async callbacks. The function returned the count right away, before any `db.put` had finished. Slow writes were still in flight when it resolved. A failed write became an unhandled rejection instead of making `saveAll` reject.

I replaced the loop with `await Promise.all(items.map((item) => db.put(item.id, item)))`. `saveAll` now resolves only after every write finishes, and it rejects if any write fails. The writes still run concurrently.

I also added two tests in `test/store.test.js`. One uses a db with delayed writes and checks that everything is saved by the time `saveAll` resolves. The other checks that a failing write makes `saveAll` reject. I didn't run the new slow-write test against the old code, so I haven't confirmed it fails there.

If your db can't handle all the writes at once, tell me and I'll make them run in sequence or in batches.
